title: Between, among; by, beside
summary: Тонкие различия между **between** и **among**, предлогами места **by / beside / next to**, а также **beside** и **besides**.
ru:
## between: каждый объект виден отдельно
**between** мы используем, когда осознаём каждый предмет, человека или точку как отдельную единицу. Их может быть двое, трое или больше — важно, что каждый «назван» или различим.
> The agreement was signed **between** Germany, France and Italy. — Соглашение подписали Германия, Франция и Италия (каждая — самостоятельная сторона).
> There are direct flights **between** Bishkek and Istanbul. — Между Бишкеком и Стамбулом есть прямые рейсы.
> I can't decide **between** the three job offers. — Не могу выбрать из трёх предложений о работе.
Between задаёт и рамки по времени и количеству: **between 9 and 11**, **between 20 and 30 people**. Второй элемент всегда вводится через **and**, а не to: ~~between 9 to 11~~ → between 9 **and** 11.

## among: внутри группы или массы
**among** показывает, что предмет находится в окружении многих и является частью группы, при этом отдельных членов группы мы не выделяем. После among идёт множественное число, неисчисляемое или собирательное существительное.
> She found the receipt **among** her old papers. — Квитанция нашлась среди старых бумаг.
> The rumour spread **among** the staff. — Слух разошёлся среди сотрудников.
> The song is very popular **among** teenagers. — Песня очень популярна у подростков.
Ещё among значит «в числе»: *Among the guests were two ministers.* — *Among other things, we discussed the budget.* Вариант **amongst** — британский и более книжный; в живой речи он встречается реже.

## Тонкости выбора
- **Раздел, распределение.** Делят *between* небольшое число названных получателей (*The money was split between the three sisters*), а *among* — многочисленную или безликую группу (*The leaflets were handed out among the crowd*).
- **Различие, выбор, связь** между двумя сторонами — только between: *the difference between*, *a choice between*, *a link between*, *a connection between*.
- **Устойчивые выражения:** **between you and me** (после предлога — me, ~~between you and I~~), **between ourselves**, **in between**, **between jobs** (временно без работы), **among friends**, **among other things**.

## by и beside: «рядом»
**by** + место означает «у, возле»: *a house by the river*, *standing by the door*. **beside** — «рядом, сбоку от»: *Come and sit beside me.* **next to** — самый нейтральный и разговорный вариант. Во многих контекстах они взаимозаменимы: *sit by / beside / next to me*.
> They have a cottage **by** the lake. — У них дача на берегу озера.
> Put the lamp **beside** the sofa. — Поставь лампу рядом с диваном.
Но у **by** гораздо больше значений, чем «рядом»: способ (*by train, by email*), деятель в пассиве (*written by*), срок (*by Friday* — об этом юнит 93), величина изменения (*rose by 10%*), **by myself** («сам, без помощи» или «в одиночестве»), **by the way** («кстати»).

## beside или besides
Одна буква, но разный смысл. **beside** — предлог места («рядом с»). **besides** — «помимо, кроме», а как наречие — «к тому же».
> **Besides** English, she speaks Kyrgyz and Russian. — Помимо английского, она говорит по-киргизски и по-русски.
> Nobody **besides** Tom knew the password. — Кроме Тома, пароль никто не знал.
> I don't feel like going out; **besides**, it's late. — Не хочется выходить; к тому же уже поздно.
Идиомы с beside: **beside the point** («не по существу»), **beside yourself with** + эмоция («вне себя от»): *He was beside himself with worry.*

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~between you and I~~ → between you and **me**
- ~~a quarrel among the two brothers~~ → a quarrel **between** the two brothers
- ~~between 5 to 6 o'clock~~ → between 5 **and** 6 o'clock
- ~~Beside English, she speaks German.~~ → **Besides** English, she speaks German.
- ~~He was besides himself with joy.~~ → He was **beside** himself with joy.
en:
## between: each item is seen as separate
We use **between** when we think of each person, thing or point as an individual unit. There may be two, three or more of them, but each one is distinct or named.
> The agreement was signed **between** Germany, France and Italy.
> There are direct flights **between** Bishkek and Istanbul.
> I can't decide **between** the three job offers.
Between also sets limits of time and quantity: **between 9 and 11**, **between 20 and 30 people**. The second element is always introduced by **and**, never to: ~~between 9 to 11~~ → between 9 **and** 11.

## among: inside a group or mass
**among** shows that something is surrounded by many others and is part of a group; we do not single out the members. It is followed by a plural, uncountable or collective noun.
> She found the receipt **among** her old papers.
> The rumour spread **among** the staff.
> The song is very popular **among** teenagers.
Among also means "included in": *Among the guests were two ministers.* *Among other things, we discussed the budget.* **Amongst** is a British, more literary variant and is less common in everyday speech.

## Choosing between them
- **Sharing and distributing.** We split things *between* a small number of named recipients (*The money was split between the three sisters*) and *among* a large or faceless group (*The leaflets were handed out among the crowd*).
- **Differences, choices and links** involving two sides take between only: *the difference between*, *a choice between*, *a link between*.
- **Fixed phrases:** **between you and me** (me after a preposition, ~~between you and I~~), **between ourselves**, **in between**, **between jobs**, **among friends**, **among other things**.

## by and beside: "near"
**by** + place means "at, next to": *a house by the river*, *standing by the door*. **beside** means "at the side of": *Come and sit beside me.* **next to** is the most neutral, everyday choice. They are often interchangeable: *sit by / beside / next to me*.
> They have a cottage **by** the lake.
> Put the lamp **beside** the sofa.
But **by** has many other uses: means (*by train, by email*), the agent in a passive sentence (*written by*), deadlines (*by Friday*, see Unit 93), the size of a change (*rose by 10%*), **by myself** ("alone" or "without help") and **by the way**.

## beside or besides
One letter, but a different meaning. **beside** is a preposition of place. **besides** means "in addition to" or "apart from", and as an adverb "what is more".
> **Besides** English, she speaks Kyrgyz and Russian.
> Nobody **besides** Tom knew the password.
> I don't feel like going out; **besides**, it's late.
Idioms with beside: **beside the point** (irrelevant) and **beside yourself with** + emotion: *He was beside himself with worry.*

## Common mistakes
- ~~between you and I~~ → between you and **me**
- ~~a quarrel among the two brothers~~ → a quarrel **between** the two brothers
- ~~between 5 to 6 o'clock~~ → between 5 **and** 6 o'clock
- ~~Beside English, she speaks German.~~ → **Besides** English, she speaks German.
- ~~He was besides himself with joy.~~ → He was **beside** himself with joy.
structure:
## Сравнение форм
| Форма | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| between | двое или больше, каждый виден отдельно; рамки | between Paris and Rome · between 3 and 5 |
| among | в окружении многих, часть группы | among the crowd · among friends |
| by | у, возле; способ; деятель в пассиве; величина | by the door · by bus · written by her · up by 5% |
| beside | рядом с, сбоку от | beside the bed |
| next to | рядом (нейтральный, разговорный) | next to the bank |
| besides | помимо, кроме; к тому же | besides Tom · Besides, it's late. |

## Формулы
> **between** + A + **and** + B
> the gap **between** rich **and** poor · **between** 1990 **and** 2000

> **among** + мн. число / неисчисляемое / группа
> **among** the passengers · **among** the evidence

> **beside** + существительное = рядом · **besides** + существительное = помимо
> **beside** the road ≠ **besides** the road

> **between you and me** (не ~~I~~) · **by myself** = alone / unaided

items.text: There is a striking similarity {{between}} the two novels.
The rumour quickly spread {{among}} the factory workers.
She found an old photograph {{among}} the papers in the drawer.
I had to choose {{between}} a higher salary and more free time.
Let's keep this {{between}} you and me.
Unemployment is high {{among}} young graduates in the region.
The bus runs {{between}} the airport and the city centre every twenty minutes.
The inheritance was divided {{among}} the forty members of the family.

exercises.title: by, beside, besides или among?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте подходящее слово. В скобках — варианты, из которых нужно выбрать.

items.text: He was {{beside}} himself with anger when he read the email.
{{Besides}} English, she speaks Kyrgyz, Russian and some Turkish.
Your comment is completely {{beside}} the point.
The novel was written {{by}} a retired physicist.
I'd rather finish the project {{by}} myself than rely on him.
Several local firms, {{among}} them the biggest bank in the region, sponsored the festival.
Nobody {{besides}} the manager has a key to the archive.
Prices went up {{by}} four per cent last quarter.

items.q: The path runs ___ two rows of old oaks.
Her name was ___ those on the shortlist.
The disagreement ___ the two managers was soon forgotten.
___ the many problems, the most serious was the lack of funding.
I'd like a seat ___ the window.
___ being cheap, the hotel is close to the sea.
Just between ___, I don't trust him.
items.why: После предлога — объектная форма: **between you and me**.

exercises.title: Перефразируйте
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя слово в скобках.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **next to**: The pharmacy is beside the post office.
answers: The pharmacy is next to the post office.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **between**: Tom was sitting with Ann on one side and Lisa on the other.
answers: Tom was sitting between Ann and Lisa.
Tom was sitting between Lisa and Ann.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **among**: The new policy is unpopular with many of our employees.
answers: The new policy is unpopular among our employees.
The new policy is unpopular among many of our employees.

items.prompt: Rewrite in the passive with **by**: A famous architect designed the library.
answers: The library was designed by a famous architect.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **by myself**: I live alone.
answers: I live by myself.

items.prompt: Rewrite with **between**: The share of women in the team is somewhere from 40 to 50 per cent.
answers: The share of women in the team is between 40 and 50 per cent.
The share of women in the team is between 40 and 50 percent.

items.prompt: Who sits next to you at work or at school? Use **beside** or **by**.
items.sample: A colleague called Aigul sits beside me at work.

items.prompt: What do you have to choose between at the moment? Use **between**.
items.sample: I have to choose between two job offers.

items.prompt: What is popular among people your age? Use **among**.
items.sample: Podcasts are very popular among my friends.

items.prompt: Is there anything you like to do by yourself?

items.prompt: Besides your native language, what other languages do you speak?
items.sample: Besides Russian, I speak English and a little German.
